name: Food taboos in pregnancy
what_people_do: Pregnant women avoid certain foods because of family rules and beliefs about the baby and about witchcraft.
why_they_say_it_works: Foods are believed to harm or mark the baby or ease labour.

documented_by.source: Traditional belief and practice among the Pokot people of Kenya, 1988, Ann Trop Paediatr, PMID 2461145
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Pokot of Kenya (1988): numerous dietary taboos; authors link them to a high rate of low birth weight.

evidence.finding: Authors suggest taboos contribute to low birth weight; not measured in a comparison.

source.name: Traditional belief and practice among the Pokot people of Kenya, 1988, Ann Trop Paediatr, PMID 2461145

harm_note: Restriction of nutritious food in pregnancy can lower birth weight, per the authors' view; 1988, one community.
gaps: A 2026 Jimma, Ethiopia qualitative study (PMID 41593435) seen as a title only.
